subject: Accounting
title: IT Controls in Modern Business
description: A fast breakdown of IT Controls in Modern Business for builders.

hook.text: Most transactions today are processed by software. If the software has a flaw, every record is wrong.

buildup.text: IT controls govern access, change management, backups, and system integrity.

discovery.text: Access controls ensure only authorized people can enter, modify, or approve transactions.

twist.text: A single developer with admin access to both the code and the production database can bypass every control.

climax.text: Auditors now test IT controls as heavily as financial ones—because the numbers depend on the systems.

punchline.text: Control the system, control the numbers.

quiz.question: Why do auditors test IT controls?
options: Because financial data depends on system integrity

details.summary: IT controls are the policies and procedures that protect information systems, ensuring data integrity, availability, and security. As businesses become fully digital, IT controls have become as critical as traditional financial controls.
details.whyItMatters: Virtually all financial data now flows through IT systems. Weak IT controls mean unreliable financial data, regardless of how strong traditional accounting controls are.
takeaways: IT general controls cover access security, change management, system operations, and data backup
Application controls are built into software to validate data input, processing, and output accuracy
Auditors must evaluate IT controls to assess whether system-generated financial data is reliable

faq.question: What are IT general controls?
faq.answer: IT general controls (ITGCs) cover technology infrastructure: access management (who can do what), change management (controlling updates), system operations (monitoring), and business continuity (backups and disaster recovery). They underpin all application-specific controls.

faq.question: Why do financial auditors care about IT controls?
faq.answer: Nearly all financial data originates from, is processed by, and is stored in IT systems. If records can be changed without authorization or calculations are unreliable, financial statements can't be trusted. IT control evaluation is now standard in every financial audit.
